def: A function treated like any other piece of data, so it can be stored in a variable, passed as an argument, returned as a result or kept in a dictionary.
A dictionary that maps names to functions, such as mutation operators, so a loop can pick one by name and call it.
A small unnamed function written as a single expression, best kept for short one-off uses such as a sort key.
An inner function that keeps using variables from the outer function that made it, even after the outer function has returned.
Python looks up a closure's captured variable when the function is called, not when it was made, so loop-built lambdas all see the final value.
Remembering the result of a function call so that a repeat call with the same arguments costs nothing, as functools.lru_cache does.
Describes a value with a fixed, unchanging hash, which lets it be a dictionary key or set member; tuples of numbers are hashable and lists are not.
A class declared with @dataclass, which writes the constructor, readable text form and equality check from its list of typed fields.
A method with a double-underscore name, such as __add__ or __lt__, that Python calls when you use an operator or built-in on your object.
An object that Python raises when something goes wrong, which travels up the callers until a matching except clause handles it.
An evaluation function that returns a score for every input and never raises, turning each crash or invalid candidate into a penalty score.
An annotation such as list[int] or Callable[[int], float] that documents intended types for readers and checkers but is not enforced at run time.
A dictionary or set that stores the candidates seen so far, keyed by a hashable field, so duplicates are noticed and the best are kept.
